--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_regular_expander()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Check whether the graph is a regular expander that meets the Ramanujan bound. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_regular_expander()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Check whether the graph is a regular expander that meets the Ramanujan bound. title: >- [Graph.is_regular_expander()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Check whether the graph is a regular expander that meets the Ramanujan bound. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check whether the graph is a regular expander that meets the Ramanujan bound. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L27600-L27749){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_regular_expander(epsilon=0.0) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is regular expander](../assets/graphs/is-regular-expander.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two 3-regular graphs on six nodes, each with its second eigenvalue, the largest one in absolute value after the degree 3, in a note above it. Left: the prism, two triangles joined by spokes, has eigenvalues down to -2, within the Ramanujan bound 2 sqrt(2), about 2.83, so is_regular_expander() returns True. Right: the complete bipartite graph K3,3, its two sides in the accent color and teal, has eigenvalue -3 because it is bipartite, past the bound, so is_regular_expander() returns False." width="100%"} A `d`-regular graph's adjacency matrix has largest eigenvalue `d`; how far the other eigenvalues stay from it, the spectral gap, measures how well the graph expands: how many edges leave every set of nodes, and how fast random walks mix. The Alon-Boppana bound says the second-largest eigenvalue in absolute value can't be much smaller than `2 sqrt(d - 1)` for large graphs, and graphs that reach it are called Ramanujan. This method returns `True` when the graph is `d`-regular for some `d >= 1` and that eigenvalue is below `2 sqrt(d - 1) + epsilon`, as NetworkX's `is_regular_expander()` does. The eigenvalues are computed exactly from the dense adjacency matrix, in time proportional to `n^3`, so the check suits graphs of up to a few thousand nodes. The graph must be undirected and simple, and edge weights are ignored. The whole graph is checked and the current selection is ignored. Checking for expansion is useful for: - verifying that a generated network (a random regular graph, a peer-to-peer overlay) has the fast mixing it was built for - confirming the output of `add_random_regular_expander_graph()` or `add_maybe_regular_expander()` - comparing explicit expander constructions with random ones ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [epsilon]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Slack added to the Ramanujan bound `2 sqrt(d - 1)`. Default is `0`. Must be non-negative. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is regular of positive degree and its second-largest absolute adjacency eigenvalue is below the bound. Graphs that aren't regular, have degree `0`, or have fewer than two nodes return `False`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or has self-loops or parallel edges, or `epsilon=` is negative. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} For a $d$-regular graph with adjacency eigenvalues $d = \lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_n$, let $\lambda = \max(|\lambda_2|, |\lambda_n|)$. The graph passes when $\lambda < 2\sqrt{d - 1} + \varepsilon$. A disconnected regular graph has $\lambda_2 = d$ and a bipartite one $\lambda_n = -d$, and since $d \ge 2\sqrt{d - 1}$ for every $d$, both fail when `epsilon=0`. So does any 2-regular graph with an even cycle, whose eigenvalue $-2$ sits exactly on the bound; a small margin keeps rounding error from passing it, as NetworkX's floating-point comparison sometimes does. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~is_regular`) : Check whether every node has the same degree. [](`~adjacency_spectrum`) : Return the adjacency eigenvalues the check is based on. [](`~add_random_regular_expander_graph`) : Draw a random regular graph that passes the check. [](`~add_margulis_gabber_galil_graph`) : Build an explicit 8-regular expander. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The Petersen graph is 3-regular with eigenvalues `3`, `1` and `-2`, so it is Ramanujan (`2 < 2 sqrt(2) ≈ 2.83`): ::: {#15b88ce9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ec.Graph().add_named_graph("petersen").is_regular_expander() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: A cycle of even length is bipartite, so `-2` is one of its eigenvalues and the bound of `2` for degree `2` fails. A star isn't regular at all: ::: {#0513faf7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} cycle = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(20) star = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5) cycle.is_regular_expander(), star.is_regular_expander() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (False, False) ``` ::: ::: Random regular graphs are almost always expanders: ::: {#48c5ab66 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} regular = ec.Graph().add_random_regular_graph(n=200, d=5, seed=1) regular.is_regular_expander() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ### A long prism or a random graph Two 3-regular graphs on `38` nodes. The prism on the left, two 19-node cycles joined by spokes, has a second eigenvalue of `1 + 2 cos(2π / 19) ≈ 2.89`, just past the bound of `2.83`, and its farthest nodes are `10` steps apart. The random 3-regular graph on the right passes, with a diameter of `7`: ::: {#cfc4d8a5 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} prism = ec.Graph().add_generalized_petersen_graph(19, 1) random_graph = ec.Graph().add_random_regular_graph(n=38, d=3, seed=1) [(g.is_regular_expander(), g.diameter()) for g in (prism, random_graph)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` [(False, 10), (True, 7)] ``` ::: ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#4904b20f .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} rings = [list(range(20, 39)), list(range(1, 20))] prism.layout_shell(nlist=rings, rotate=0).plot( layout="pos", show_labels=False, node_size=6, width=320, height=320, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
